text:
SRE-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: multiple tokenizer-preproc pods OOMKilled on prod-eu around 03:11 UTC. Pager fired to #incidents (severity: page).

Maria G: paging in. seeing repeated OOMKills on tokenizer-preproc replicas (v2.1). CPU and RSS on those containers climb quickly then get killed by the kubelet. Node: ip-10-0-4-12.

Jonah H: looking at logs now — decode workers on some GPU pods show `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` shortly after the preproc spike. could be coincident or memory corruption triggered by the preproc overload.

Maria G: quick outputs:
```
$ kubectl get pods -n prod | grep tokenizer-preproc
tokenizer-preproc-5f8d9   0/1   OOMKilled   0   21m
tokenizer-preproc-6c9a1   0/1   OOMKilled   0   20m

$ kubectl describe pod tokenizer-preproc-5f8d9 -n prod
Events:
  Type    Reason     Age   From               Message
  ----    ------     ----  ----               -------
  Warning OOMKilling 2m    kubelet, ip-10-0-4-12   Container killed due to memory usage
```

Maria G: also seeing huge thread counts in the proc for the tokenizer process (sudden fanout when parse fails). suspect runaway tokenization for extremely long prompts.

Jonah H: grabbing node-level dmesg and journal. found repeated `nvidia: GPU fault` and `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` around 03:11:07. snippet: 
```
Mar 15 03:11:07 ip-10-0-4-12 kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus.
Mar 15 03:11:08 ip-10-0-4-12 kubelet: Container runtime error: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = containerd: container did not start: exit status 137
```

eng-runtime-oncall: taking action — cordoning node ip-10-0-4-12 and evicting non-daemonset pods.
`kubectl cordon ip-10-0-4-12 && kubectl drain ip-10-0-4-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`

Maria G: scaled tokenizer-preproc down to 0 to stop the immediate fanout and restarted with a conservative env var: `TOKENIZER_MAX_WORKERS=8` to limit thread spawning. rolling restart applied to preproc daemonset.

ops-runbooks-bot: Runbook: https://runbooks.internal/redwood/tokenizer-high-cpu (recommended mitigations: throttle incoming prompt length, set TOKENIZER_MAX_WORKERS, cordon/drain affected nodes, enable fallback routing).

Jonah H: applied routing change — for heavy prompt customers in EU we enabled fallback to model-compact-1 for 30m to reduce end-to-end work. This should cut load on tokenizer by ~60%.

Maria G: initial impact estimate: 03:10:30–03:28:00 UTC saw a 5xx spike; roughly 3.2% of requests returned 5xx or timeouts. Enterprise-cust-42 in EU saw elevated error rates and latency; support has been notified. No PII exposed, no data loss. :thumbsup:

eng-runtime-oncall: mitigation status: cordoned node, preproc scaled/restarted with conservative config, routing fallback in place. Monitoring: error rate trending down but still above baseline — continuing to watch.

Jonah H: next troubleshooting steps Im kicking off: collect core dumps from any crashy gpu pods (if available), capture `nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,Utilization` outputs, and pull kernel logs for the window. Suspect a correlation between tokenization fanout (CPU OOMs) and GPU fault surfacing later.

Maria G: handoff to morning eng-sre: @eng-runtime-oncall please own immediate follow-up with infra for node replacement and kernel/driver checks. I'll continue to monitor for 15 more mins and then hand off formally. :ambulance:

Leah C: taking handoff at 03:30 UTC. brief summary sent to #incidents-updates and support. I'll coordinate postmortem and customer comms. Owner: Leah C (postmortem), Jonah H (driver/gpu investigation), Maria G (short-term mitigations).

eng-runtime-oncall: created incident ticket INC-2026-0452 and attached time-series graphs (CPU, memory, 5xx rates) and affected tenant list.

Maria G: notes for postmortem: collect sample prompts from the time window (redact PII), evaluate tokenizer's worst-case complexity on malformed prompts, add protective limits in routing layer to reject or queue extremely long prompts, and consider backpressure from gateway into preproc.

Leah C: ETA for postmortem doc: EOD tomorrow. Immediate followups: schedule kernel/driver repro with infra (Jonah), add a temporary server-side prompt length cap for prod-eu (Maria), and escalate to Dedicated infra if we see hardware fault patterns.

Maria G: closing loop — system stable for now, error rates returned near baseline after routing fallback. will keep the cordon for at least one full deployment cycle.

eng-runtime-oncall: final note: if we see recurrence, escalate to infra on-call to provision replacement nodes and consider fleet-wide driver roll.

SRE-bot: Incident acknowledged and recorded. :white_check_mark:
